Check the ingredients and nutrition facts. Habaneros, ghost peppers, etc will give you a good kick in the face. Too much sugar will fuck up the salsa and make it too sweet. Too much fat will dilute the spiciness. For example, avocado salsa tastes great, but its hard to make a spicy version.

You can always modify your store bought salsas. If its too thick, and you font want to kill the spiciness to much, you can mix in vinegar or alcohol. If its to thin, and you want to bring down the spiciness, you can add olive oil. You can always toss in tomatoes and onion to taste. Feel free to incorporate your own spices. I love ginger so I mix it into every salsa I buy. Your salsas at your local hispanic-centric store will have good salsas. Likewise your asian-centric store should have a good selection of spicy sauces.

You can always mix in hot sauce! It'll thin out your salsa, but it can add a nice kick.
